s1.publisher: Cayman Islands Department of Tourism (Explore Cayman)
s1.quote: The top of the wreck is at a depth of about 20 feet and the bottom at a depth of about 80 feet … The ship is approximately 330 feet (100 meters) long

s2.quote: MV Captain Keith Tibbetts wreck … The site starts at 30 feet (10 m), but rests at 90 feet (30 m) … There’s usually little to no current and 90- to 100-foot (30 to 33 m) visibility

highlights.text: 330 ft ex-Cuban Navy frigate with intact guns
Sponge-covered hull; turtles, barracuda, groupers

hazards.text: Mid-section and stern storm-damaged: tangled structure

summary.text: A 330 ft former Soviet-built frigate sunk in 1996 off Cayman Brac as an artificial reef. It sits between about 20 and 90 ft, is covered in sponges, and storm damage has opened the structure up while leaving guns and the bow's red star.

sites.name: Jackson Wall and Reef - Grand Cayman

s1.quote: Jackson Reef / Wall / The Meadows This site is shore accessible and features mini-walls with swim-throughs and plenty of large fish as well as the occasional ray

s2.quote: Jackson’s Reef … healthy reefs start at about 30 feet (10 m). There’s little to no current and visibility can reach 100 feet in winter (33 m) and up to 200 feet (66 m) in summer

highlights.text: Mini-walls with swim-throughs
Turtles, rays, reef sharks and barracuda
Large fish and occasional rays

sites.name: Bloody Bay Wall

s1.quote: Bloody Bay Wall Marine Park, possibly the best diving area in all of the Caribbean! Ranging in depth from 20 to over 5,000 feet deep, the wall is alive with a variety of corals and colourful sponges, tubes and fans

s2.publisher: Cayman Islands Department of Tourism (Explore Cayman)
s2.quote: Bloody Bay Wall in Little Cayman … Situated along the north shore of Little Cayman, the drop off plunges to staggering depths, reaching over 1,000 meters

s3.quote: Most are on the edge of one of the Caribbean’s deepest drop-offs of approximately 6,000 feet (2,000 m)

sites.depthNote: Wall top about 20 ft; drops thousands of feet

highlights.text: Sheer wall with sponges, tubes and gorgonian fans
Large fish, rays and sharks
Turtles and Nassau groupers

summary.text: A sheer wall along Little Cayman's north shore that starts at about 20 ft and falls thousands of feet. Coral, sponges and fans cover the face, and turtles, groupers, rays and sharks cruise past in very clear water.

s1.quote: newly named moored sites, Turtle Alley … the mid-reef in 45 to 55 feet of water was rich with barrel and row pore rope sponges as well as the gorgonians typical of deeper reefs with a bit of current flow

highlights.text: Barrel and rope sponges, gorgonians on mid-reef

s1.quote: East Chute and what used to be the wreck of the Cayman Mariner … The vertical face of the wall begins at about 70 feet, and large coral mounds surrounding the valley rise to about 45 feet

summary.text: A North Wall classic where a freestanding pinnacle rises from over 100 ft to within 45 ft of the surface, set tight against the main wall. The gap between is full of black coral and gorgonians, and the dive is easy enough for first-time ocean divers.
